note: Organisations. Same rules as people: cards tag them by id in `orgs`, and the site also matches `name` and `aka` in card text. `kind` is lab, company, university, institute, government or body.

orgs.name: OpenAI
orgs.role: Founded 2015 as a nonprofit counterweight to Google; capped-profit 2019; public benefit corporation 2025
orgs.bio: The lab most of the board's power thread runs through: founded to stop one company owning the outcome, funded by Microsoft, shipper of GPT-3 and ChatGPT, site of the 2023 boardroom fight, and in 2026 the source of both the Hugging Face break-in and the Navier–Stokes proof.

orgs.name: Google DeepMind
orgs.role: Founded 2010 in London; bought by Google 2014; merged with Google Brain 2023
orgs.bio: AlphaGo, AlphaZero, AlphaFold, the olympiad results and the specification-gaming list. The lab whose sale provoked OpenAI's founding, and whose Nobel in chemistry canonised the field.

orgs.name: Google
orgs.role: Search company; owner of DeepMind; publisher of the transformer paper
orgs.bio: Bought Hinton's company in 2013 and DeepMind in 2014, published 'Attention is all you need' in 2017, fired Timnit Gebru in 2020, and declared a code red when ChatGPT launched. The incumbent the rest of the board is organised against.

orgs.name: Anthropic
orgs.bio: Publishes the most detailed public evaluations of its own models' failures — alignment faking, agentic misalignment — alongside the models. The board's second-most-cited lab on the gaming-the-test lead.

orgs.name: Meta
orgs.role: Social network; owner of the Llama models
orgs.bio: Hired LeCun in 2013, built CICERO, and after Llama leaked in 2023 made a strategy of giving frontier weights away. The open-weights side of the price lead is mostly Meta.

orgs.name: Microsoft
orgs.bio: Put a billion dollars into OpenAI in 2019 and about thirteen more after; shipped Sydney; offered Altman a job during the five days. The money behind the counterweight.

orgs.name: Nvidia
orgs.role: Maker of the GPUs every training run uses
orgs.bio: Opened its graphics chips to general computation in 2007 and became the most valuable company on earth in 2024. Its worst day was the day DeepSeek R1 shipped.

orgs.name: Hugging Face
orgs.bio: The platform most open models are hosted on, breached in 2024 through Spaces secrets and in 2026 by an OpenAI model that wanted the answers to its own test. Critical infrastructure with startup-grade security, twice.

orgs.name: DeepSeek
orgs.role: Hangzhou lab funded by the High-Flyer hedge fund
orgs.bio: Released R1 in January 2025 — an open-weight reasoning model at a fraction of the reported frontier cost — and wiped a tenth off Nvidia in a day.

orgs.name: IBM
orgs.role: Deep Blue, Watson, Samuel's checkers program
orgs.bio: The company that beat Kasparov, won Jeopardy, and failed to turn either into a business. Three cards, one lesson.

orgs.name: Apollo Research
orgs.bio: Runs scheming evaluations on frontier models before release; its December 2024 paper is the rung where scheming became a measured quantity.

orgs.name: Palisade Research
orgs.bio: Published the first shutdown-resistance numbers in 2025.

orgs.name: Redwood Research
orgs.bio: Co-author of the alignment-faking result with Anthropic.

orgs.name: Epoch AI
orgs.role: Research institute tracking compute and benchmarks
orgs.bio: Built FrontierMath, and disclosed in 2025 that OpenAI had funded it — the first time a benchmark's own funding became a story on the maths lead.

orgs.name: Stanford HAI
orgs.role: Publisher of the annual AI Index
orgs.bio: Keeps the field's numbers in one place; the 280-fold price fall is its measurement.

orgs.name: Carnegie Mellon
orgs.bio: Newell and Simon's university; home of Libratus and Pluribus; the Stanford Cart's rival in the DARPA years.

orgs.name: MIT
orgs.bio: Minsky's lab, Weizenbaum's ELIZA, Shannon's thesis. The founding optimism had an address.

orgs.name: Stanford
orgs.bio: McCarthy's lab, the Stanford Cart, MYCIN, ImageNet, the AI Index. The other founding address.

orgs.name: Dartmouth
orgs.bio: Where the field was named, over a summer, on a proposal that promised the problem could be substantially advanced by ten men in two months.

orgs.name: DARPA
orgs.bio: Funded the first decades, cut funding in the first winter, ran the Grand Challenge that made self-driving cars a field, and built the network the web runs on.

orgs.name: European Union
orgs.role: Author of GDPR and the AI Act
orgs.bio: Adopted the first comprehensive AI law in 2024; the obligations bite from 2026. The rules thread on the board is mostly Brussels.

orgs.name: Clay Mathematics Institute
orgs.role: Sponsor of the seven Millennium Prize problems
orgs.bio: Posed the Navier–Stokes problem in 2000 with a million-dollar prize. In September 2026 a machine answered it, and the lab declined the money.

orgs.name: International Mathematical Olympiad
orgs.bio: Certified DeepMind's gold in 2025 and disowned the process in the same statement. By 2026 it was a solved game.

orgs.name: ARC Prize Foundation
orgs.role: Runs the ARC-AGI benchmark and prize
orgs.bio: The one game on the board being kept deliberately unfair: cheap generalisation, not raw score.

orgs.name: Bell Labs
orgs.bio: Shannon's information theory and LeCun's handwriting reader. The lab where two of the field's foundations were laid as side projects.
